note: Published claims about 2010 KQ = RK252A5 and the candidate launches, used only for comparison (nothing here enters the fit).

deletion.reason: non-gravitational motion (Liverpool Telescope astrometry to July 6)

gray_2010_07_06.note: uses Miles's June 26 and July 6 astrometry (not public); reported in Miles 2011 as Gray, private communication
gray_2010_07_06.source: R. Miles, J. Br. Astron. Assoc. 121, 350 (2011)

miles_2011.spectrum: matches UV-weathered white titanium-dioxide paint (LDEF Chemglaze A276), not any asteroid class
miles_2011.conclusion: highly likely the final rocket stage of a Russian moon probe: Luna 1, Luna 4 or Luna 23

helios1_centaur.label: Helios 1 Centaur TC-2 (1974-097C)
helios1_centaur.status: ruled out before this study: the Centaur extended mission left it in Earth orbit (158,700 x 1,760 km) and it re-entered in 1979 (J. Hopkins, cited by Miles 2011)

luna1.label: Luna 1 Blok-E stage
luna1.orbit: heliocentric 0.978 x 1.318 AU, 450 d (Miles 2011, from the RAE tables)

luna4.label: Luna 4 Blok-L stage
luna4.orbit: missed the Moon by about 8,500 km on 1963-04-05 into an Earth orbit of 89,250 x 694,000 km (RAE table 1963)
luna4.size_m: 2.7 diameter x 2.7 long; A/m about 0.0077 m^2/kg (Miles 2011)

luna23.label: Luna 23 Blok-D stage
luna23.stage: Blok D: 3.7 m diameter, about 5.7-6.3 m long, 2.1-2.5 t empty
